newsitem.title: BURMA: Malaysia Foreign Minister meets top Burma general.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Foreign Minister meets top Burma general.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi met Burma's prime minister General Than Shwe during a visit to Rangoon on Monday, the Myanmar News Agency (MNA) reported.
MNA did not give any details of the meeting, but the two had been expected to discuss issues related to Burma's application to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Burma has applied for full membership to the seven-nation ASEAN which groups Brunei, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam in addition to Malaysia.

Philippine President Fidel Ramos said earlier this month that ASEAN might review its policy of "constructive engagement" with Rangoon after the military regime renewed a crackdown on the democracy movement led by Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

The question of Burma's membership will be discussed at a meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers in Manila on November 20 and will also be addressed at an informal summit of ASEAN leaders in Jakarta on November 30.
Malaysia has said it will maintain its relations with the Burmese military government despite the recent crackdown.
Trade relations between the two nations have risen lately, and Malaysia is now the fifth largest foreign investor in Burma.
Official Burmese statistics show total Malaysian investment through July was $420 million.
